methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier, a seed-stage transportation company founded by Sampriti Bhattacharyya, has raised $7.2M to date. The broader transportation sector contains three private peers of note—Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride—though none operate at identical stage or valuation proximity, limiting direct peer benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement. Using the $7.2M total raised as a proxy base value, this method yields an implied valuation of $18M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector; applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M, centered at $18M. The spread reflects inherent uncertainty in stage-progression multiples for frontier transportation ventures, which can vary materially based on capital efficiency, IP defensibility, and go-to-market readiness. The primary limitation is the absence of granular peer data at seed stage in transportation; materialization of this range depends on confirmatory diligence around product-market fit, funding runway, and competitive positioning relative to the broader cohort.
